stories.title: Christa Pike Discharged From Hospital After Failed Execution

Kanlaon on Negros Island produced a moderately explosive eruption on Saturday, Oct. 10, sending an ash plume above its summit, according to the Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology (Phivolcs). In an advisory, Phivolcs said the eruption began shortly before 12:30 p.m. and ended at 12:48 p.m. Kanlaon Volcano remains under Alert

stories.title: We can’t help treating AI like it’s human. But should we?
stories.summary: People readily treat even simple AI exchanges as if a caring relationship exists, raising questions about whether that instinct should be encouraged. Sherry Turkle argues that users can believe a relational artefact cares for them and are then psychologically inclined to care for it in return.

links.headline: We can’t help treating AI like it’s human. But should we?
links.excerpt: "When we are drawn into even the most primitive exchanges with a relational artifact, we believe it cares for us," Dr. Sherry Turkle writes. "And we are wired to care for it in return."

stories.title: ‘This is not an anti-tech town’: backlash to datacenter in city once home to IBM
stories.summary: Residents of East Fishkill, New York, are fighting a proposed data centre as communities weigh AI’s promised benefits against its substantial costs. The dispute is unfolding in a town with deep technology roots: a 460-acre local campus housed IBM semiconductor research and manufacturing for nearly 50 years.

links.headline: ‘This is not an anti-tech town’: backlash to datacenter in city once home to IBM
links.excerpt: Fight in East Fishkill, New York, part of a growing divide over whether AI benefits outweigh enormous downsides For decades, East Fishkill helped build New York’s tech industry. stories.title: Who owns ‘brain rot’? Inside the international legal drama over a beloved meme
stories.summary: An international legal fight over the “brain rot” character Tung Tung Tung Sahur could test where human creativity ends and artificial intelligence begins. The dispute is complicated by United States copyright law, which protects only human-made creations, while the meme belongs to an absurdist genre of AI-generated online video.
